text: Let the domain of the function $f(x)=\log _{3}\log _{5}\log _{7}\left (9x-x^{2}-13\right )$ be the interval $(\mathrm{m},\mathrm{n})$. Let the hyperbola $\frac{x^{2}}{\mathrm{a}^{2}}-\frac{y^{2}}{\mathrm{b}^{2}}=1$ have eccentricity $\frac{\mathrm{n}}{3}$ and the length of the latus rectum $\frac{8\mathrm{m}}{3}$. Then $\mathrm{b}^{2}-\mathrm{a}^{2}$ is equal to :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 23rd January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$\begin{array}{l} \log _{5}\left (\log _{7}\left (9x-x^{2}-13\right )\right )>0 \\ \Rightarrow 9x-x^{2}-13>7 \\ \Rightarrow x\in (4,5)=(m,n) \\ \Rightarrow \text{eccentricity}=\dfrac{5}{3} \\ L(LR)=\dfrac{32}{3} \\ \dfrac{25}{9}=1+\dfrac{b^{2}}{a^{2}}...(1) \end{array}$

$\begin{array}{l} \dfrac{2b^{2}}{a}=\dfrac{32}{3}\Rightarrow b^{2}=\dfrac{16a}{3} \\ \text{Substitute in (1)} \\ \begin{array}{l} \dfrac{16}{9}=\dfrac{16a}{3a^{2}}\Rightarrow a=3 \\ b^{2}=16 \\ \therefore b^{2}-a^{2}=16-9 \\ =7 \end{array} \end{array}$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2026 (Online) 23rd January Morning Shift

text: A rectangle is formed by the lines $x=0,y=0,x=3$ and $y=4$. Let the line L be perpendicular to $3x+y+6=0$ and divide the area of the rectangle into two equal parts. Then the distance of the point $\left (\frac{1}{2},-5\right )$ from the line $L$ is equal to :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 23rd January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)
tags: straight lines and pair of straight lines

solution.body:
[IMG]

For $L$ to bisect area, line must pass through the centre of rectangle $\left (\frac{3}{2},2\right )$

$\begin{array}{l} \Rightarrow L\equiv (y-2)=\dfrac{1}{3}\left (x-\dfrac{3}{2}\right ) \\ \Rightarrow 3y-6=x-\dfrac{3}{2}\Rightarrow 6y-12=2x-3 \\ 6y-2x-9=0 \end{array}$

The distance from $L$ of $\left (\frac{1}{2},-5\right )$ is

$\begin{array}{l} \left |\dfrac{6(-5)-2\left (\frac{1}{2}\right )-9}{\sqrt{40}}\right |=\sqrt{40} \\ =2\sqrt{10} \end{array}$

text:
Let the direction cosines of two lines satisfy the equations : $4l+m-n=0$ and $2mn+10nl+3lm=0$.

Then the cosine of the acute angle between these lines is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 23rd January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
From $4l+m-n=0$, $n=4l+m$. Substituting in $2mn+10nl+3lm=0$:

$2m(4l+m)+10l(4l+m)+3lm=0\Rightarrow 40l^{2}+21lm+2m^{2}=0\Rightarrow (8l+m)(5l+2m)=0$

First line: $m=-8l$, so $n=4l-8l=-4l$; its direction ratios are $(1,-8,-4)$, of magnitude $\sqrt{1+64+16}=9$.

Second line: $m=-\dfrac{5l}{2}$, so $n=4l-\dfrac{5l}{2}=\dfrac{3l}{2}$; its direction ratios are $(2,-5,3)$, of magnitude $\sqrt{4+25+9}=\sqrt{38}$.

For the acute angle $θ$ between the lines,

$\cos θ=\dfrac{|(1)(2)+(-8)(-5)+(-4)(3)|}{9\sqrt{38}}=\dfrac{30}{9\sqrt{38}}=\dfrac{10}{3\sqrt{38}}$

Hence, the correct option is (C).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2026 (Online) 23rd January Morning Shift

sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 23rd January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body: $\begin{array}{l} \begin{array}{l} (-2+\sqrt{3})(|\sqrt{x}-3|)+(x-6\sqrt{x}+9)-2\sqrt{3}=0,x\geq 0 \\ \text{put}|\sqrt{x}-3|=t \\ \Rightarrow (-2+\sqrt{3})t+t^{2}-2\sqrt{3}=0 \\ \Rightarrow t(t-2)+\sqrt{3}(t-2)=0 \\ \Rightarrow (t+\sqrt{3})(t-2)=0 \\ t+\sqrt{3}\neq 0\Rightarrow t=2 \\ \Rightarrow |\sqrt{x}-3|=2 \\ \sqrt{x}-3=\pm 2 \\ \sqrt{x}=5,1 \\ x=25,1 \\ \Rightarrow α=1,β=25 \\ \Rightarrow \sqrt{\dfrac{β}{α}}+\sqrt{αβ}=10 \end{array} \\ \text{Option (2) is Correct.} \end{array}$

text: Let $f(x)=\int \frac{\left (2-x^{2}\right )\cdot \mathrm{e}^{x}}{(\sqrt{1+x})(1-x)^{3/2}}\mathrm{d}x$. If $f(0)=0$, then $f\left (\frac{1}{2}\right )$ is equal to:
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 23rd January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$f(x)=\int \frac{\left (2-x^{2}\right )\cdot e^{x}}{(\sqrt{1+x})(1-x)^{3/2}}dx$

$\Rightarrow$ $f(x)=\int \frac{\left (2-x^{2}\right )e^{x}}{\sqrt{1+x}\sqrt{1-x}(1-x)}dx$

$f(x)=\int \frac{\left (2-x^{2}\right )\cdot e^{x}}{\left (\sqrt{1-x^{2}}\right )(1-x)}dx$

$\begin{array}{l} =\int \dfrac{\left [1+\left (1-x^{2}\right )\right ]e^{x}}{\left (\sqrt{1-x^{2}}\right )(1-x)}dx \\ =\int e^{x}\left [\dfrac{1}{\left (\sqrt{1-x^{2}}\right )(1-x)}+\dfrac{1+x}{\sqrt{1-x^{2}}}\right ]dx \end{array}$

This integral is of the form $\int e^{x}[g(x)+g^{'}(x)]dx=e^{x}\cdot g(x)+C$ 

Let $g(x)=\frac{1+x}{\sqrt{1-x^{2}}}$

$g^{'}(x)=\frac{(1+x)^{'}\cdot \sqrt{1-x^{2}}-(1+x)\left (\sqrt{1-x^{2}}\right )^{'}}{\left (\sqrt{1-x^{2}}\right )^{2}}$

$=\frac{\sqrt{1-x^{2}}+\frac{\left (x2+x\right )}{\sqrt{1-x2}}}{1-x^{2}}$

$=\frac{1-x^{2}+x^{2}+x}{\sqrt{1-x^{2}}(1-x^{2})}$

$=\frac{(x+1)}{\sqrt{1-x^{2}}(1-x)(1+x)}$

$=\frac{1}{\left (\sqrt{1-x^{2}}\right )(1-x)}$

So value of integral

$f(x)=\frac{e^{x}\cdot (1+x)}{\sqrt{1-x^{2}}}+C$

Apply initial condition $f(0)=0$ to find $C$

$0=\frac{e^{0}(1+0)}{\sqrt{1-0}}+C\Rightarrow C=-1$

$\Rightarrow$ $f(x)=\frac{e^{x}(1+x)}{\sqrt{1-x^{2}}}-1$

$\therefore$ $f(1/2)=\frac{e^{1/2}(1+1/2)}{\sqrt{1-(1/2)^{2}}}-1$

$=\frac{\sqrt{e}\cdot \frac{3}{2}}{\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}}-1=\sqrt{3e}-1$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2026 (Online) 23rd January Morning Shift

text: The vertices B and C of a triangle ABC lie on the line $\frac{x}{1}=\frac{1-y}{-2}=\frac{\mathrm{z}-2}{3}$. The coordinates of A and $B$ are $(1,6,3)$ and $(4,9,α)$ respectively and $C$ is at a distance of 10 units from $B$. The area (in sq. units) of $△ABC$ is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 23rd January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
The line is $\dfrac{x}{1}=\dfrac{y-1}{2}=\dfrac{z-2}{3}$, with direction $⃗{d}=\hat{i}+2\hat{j}+3\hat{k}$ and $|⃗{d}|=\sqrt{14}$.

$B(4,9,α)$ lies on it, so $\dfrac{4}{1}=\dfrac{9-1}{2}=\dfrac{α-2}{3}$, giving $α=14$ and $B(4,9,14)$.

$B$ and $C$ lie on the line with $BC=10$, so the area is $\dfrac{1}{2}\times BC\times h$, where $h$ is the distance of $A$ from the line.

$BA\leftarrow =(1-4)\hat{i}+(6-9)\hat{j}+(3-14)\hat{k}=-3\hat{i}-3\hat{j}-11\hat{k}$, so

$BA\leftarrow \times ⃗{d}=\left |\begin{array}{lll} \hat{i} & \hat{j} & \hat{k} \\ -3 & -3 & -11 \\ 1 & 2 & 3 \end{array}\right |=13\hat{i}-2\hat{j}-3\hat{k}$

$h=\dfrac{|BA\leftarrow \times ⃗{d}|}{|⃗{d}|}=\dfrac{\sqrt{169+4+9}}{\sqrt{14}}=\sqrt{\dfrac{182}{14}}=\sqrt{13}$

$\text{Area}=\dfrac{1}{2}\times 10\times \sqrt{13}=5\sqrt{13}$

Hence, the correct option is (B).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2026 (Online) 23rd January Morning Shift

text:
Let the mean and variance of 8 numbers $-10,-7,-1,x,y,9,2,16$ be $\frac{7}{2}$ and $\frac{293}{4}$, respectively.

Then the mean of 4 numbers $x,y,x+y+1,|x-y|$ is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 23rd January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$\begin{array}{l} \text{Mean}=\dfrac{7}{2} \\ \dfrac{-10-7-1+x+y+16+2+9}{8}=\dfrac{7}{2} \\ \Rightarrow \mathrm{x}+\mathrm{y}+9=28 \\ \Rightarrow x+y=19 \\ \text{Variance}=\dfrac{293}{4} \\ \dfrac{100+49+1+x^{2}+y^{2}+256+4+81}{8}-\dfrac{49}{4}=\dfrac{293}{4} \\ \dfrac{491+x^{2}+y^{2}}{8}=\dfrac{342}{4} \\ x^{2}+y^{2}=193 \end{array}$

$\begin{array}{l} \Rightarrow (x,y)=(7,12)\text{or}(12,7) \\ \text{Mean}=\dfrac{x+y+x+y+1+|x-y|}{4} \\ =\dfrac{19+20+5}{4} \\ =11 \end{array}$

text: Number of solutions of $\sqrt{3}\cos 2θ+8\cos θ+3\sqrt{3}=0,θ\in [-3π,2π]$ is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 23rd January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Given, trigonometric equation is

$\sqrt{3}\cos 2θ+8\cos θ+3\sqrt{3}=0,θ\in [-3π,2π]$

$\Rightarrow \sqrt{3}\left (2\cos ^{2}θ-1\right )+8\cos θ+3\sqrt{3}=0$

$\Rightarrow 2\sqrt{3}\cos ^{2}θ+8\cos θ+2\sqrt{3}=0$

$\Rightarrow (\sqrt{3}\cos θ+1)(\cos θ+\sqrt{3})=0$

$\therefore \cos θ=-\sqrt{3}$  (Not possible because $-1\leq \cos θ\leq 1$)

$\therefore \cos θ=\dfrac{-1}{\sqrt{3}}$


[IMG]


Hence, $θ$ will have 5 values in $[-3π,2π]$.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2026 (Online) 23rd January Morning Shift

Let $α$ and $β$ respectively be the maximum and the minimum values of the function $f(θ)=4\left (\sin ^{4}\left (\frac{7π}{2}-θ\right )+\sin ^{4}(11π+θ)\right )-2\left (\sin ^{6}\left (\frac{3π}{2}-θ\right )+\sin ^{6}(9π-θ)\right ),θ\in 𝐑$.

Then $α+2β$ is equal to :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 23rd January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body: $\begin{array}{l} f(θ)=4\left (\sin ^{4}\left (\dfrac{7π}{2}-θ\right )+\sin ^{4}(11π+θ)\right ) \\ -2\left (\sin ^{6}\left (\dfrac{3π}{2}-θ\right )+\sin ^{6}(9π-θ)\right ) \\ =4\left (\cos ^{4}θ+\sin ^{4}θ\right )-2\left (\cos ^{6}θ+\sin ^{6}θ\right ) \\ =4\left (1-2\sin ^{2}θ\cos ^{2}θ\right ) \\ -2(1)\left (\sin ^{4}θ+\cos ^{4}θ-\sin ^{2}θ\cos ^{2}θ\right ) \\ =4-8\sin ^{2}θ\cos ^{2}θ-2\left (1-3\sin ^{2}θ\cos ^{2}θ\right ) \\ =2-2\sin ^{2}θ\cos ^{2}θ \\ =2-\dfrac{(\sin 2θ)^{2}}{2} \\ f(θ)_{\max }=2=αf(θ)_{\min }=2-\dfrac{1}{2}=\dfrac{3}{2}=β \\ α+2β=2+3=5 \end{array}$

text: Let $\vec{\mathrm{a}}=-\hat{i}+\hat{j}+2\hat{k},\mathrm{b}\leftarrow =\hat{i}-\hat{j}-3\hat{k},\vec{\mathrm{c}}=\vec{\mathrm{a}}\times \vec{\mathrm{b}}$ and $\vec{\mathrm{d}}=\vec{\mathrm{c}}\times \vec{\mathrm{a}}$. Then $(⃗{a}-⃗{b})\cdot ⃗{d}$ is equal to :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 23rd January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body: $\begin{array}{l} \begin{array}{l} (⃗{a}-⃗{b})\cdot ⃗{d}=⃗{a}\cdot ⃗{d}-⃗{b}\cdot ⃗{d} \\ \because ⃗{d}=⃗{c}\times ⃗{a}\Rightarrow ⃗{a}\cdot ⃗{d}=[⃗{a}⃗{c}⃗{a}]=0 \\ \text{And}⃗{b}\cdot ⃗{d}=⃗{b}\cdot (⃗{c}\times ⃗{a}) \\ =⃗{b}\cdot ((⃗{a}\times ⃗{b})\times ⃗{a}) \\ \Rightarrow (⃗{a}-⃗{b})\cdot ⃗{d}=⃗{b}\cdot (⃗{a}\times (⃗{a}\times ⃗{b})) \\ =⃗{b}\cdot [⃗{a}\cdot ⃗{b}⃗{a}-⃗{a}\cdot ⃗{a}⃗{b}] \\ =(⃗{a}\cdot ⃗{b})^{2}-(⃗{a}\cdot ⃗{a})(⃗{b}\cdot ⃗{b}) \\ =(-8)^{2}-6\times 11=64-66=-2 \end{array} \\ \text{Option (2) is correct.} \end{array}$

text: A building construction work can be completed by two masons A and B together in 22.5 days. Mason A alone can complete the construction work in 24 days less than mason B alone. Then mason A alone will complete the construction work in :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 23rd January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$\text{Let B’s time}=x\text{days}$

$\begin{array}{l} \Rightarrow \text{A’s time}=(x-24)\text{days} \\ \text{Rate of}\mathrm{A}=\dfrac{1}{x-24} \\ \text{Rate of}\mathrm{B}=\dfrac{1}{x} \\ \dfrac{1}{x-24}+\dfrac{1}{x}=\dfrac{1}{22.5} \\ \dfrac{2x-24}{x(x-24)}=\dfrac{1}{22.5} \\ 45x-540=x^{2}-24x \\ x^{2}-69x+540=0 \\ (x-60)(x-9)=0 \\ \Rightarrow x=60 \\ \text{A’s time}=60-24 \\ =36\text{days} \end{array}$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2026 (Online) 23rd January Morning Shift

$\begin{array}{lllllllllllll} \begin{array}{lllllll} \because q=\left |\begin{array}{lll} 0 & 1 & -2 \\ -1 & 0 & -3 \\ 3 & -1 & -1 \end{array}\right |=-10-2=-12 \\ \text{And}-p+q=\left |\begin{array}{lll} 0 & 0 & -3 \\ -2 & -3 & -6 \\ 2 & -3 & -3 \end{array}\right |=-36 \\ \Rightarrow p=q+36=24 \\ \Rightarrow p^{2}\neq 196q^{2} \end{array} \\ \text{Option (2) is correct.} \end{array}$

text: Let the line $y-x=1$ intersect the ellipse $\frac{x^{2}}{2}+\frac{y^{2}}{1}=1$ at the points A and B . Then the angle made by the line segment AB at the center of the ellipse is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 23rd January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Given equation of line is $y=x+1$ …(i)

and equation of ellipse is $\frac{x^{2}}{2}+\frac{y^{2}}{1}=1$ …(ii)


[IMG]

Since, Eq. (i) intersect Eq. (ii), then

$\frac{x^{2}}{2}+(x+1)^{2}=1\to x^{2}+2x^{2}+4x=0$

$\Rightarrow$ $x=0,-\frac{4}{3}$

$\therefore$ $y=1,-\frac{1}{3}$

Hence, points $A$ and $B$ are $(0,1)$ and $\left (-\frac{4}{3},-\frac{1}{3}\right )$,

respectively.

Now, slope of $OB=m_{OB}=\tan θ=\frac{-\frac{1}{3}}{-\frac{4}{3}}=\frac{1}{4}$

$\Rightarrow$ $θ=\tan ^{-1}\left (\frac{1}{4}\right )$

Hence, $\angle AOB=90^{\circ }+\tan ^{-1}\left (\frac{1}{4}\right )$

$=\frac{π}{2}+\tan ^{-1}\left (\frac{1}{4}\right )$

text: The sum of all possible values of $𝐧\in 𝐍$, so that the coefficients of $x,x^{2}$ and $x^{3}$ in the expansion of $\left (1+x^{2}\right )^{2}(1+x)^{\mathrm{n}}$, are in arithmetic progression is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 23rd January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body: $\begin{array}{l} \left (1+x^{2}\right )^{2}(1+x)^{n} \\ \left (1+x^{4}+2x^{2}\right )(1+x)^{n} \\ \text{Coeff of}x={}^{n}C_{1} \\ \text{Coeff of}x^{2}={}^{n}C_{2}+2\cdot {}^{n}C_{0} \\ \text{Coeff of}x^{3}={}^{n}C_{3}+2\cdot {}^{n}C_{1} \\ \because \text{Coeff of}x,x^{2},x^{3}\to \mathrm{AP} \\ \Rightarrow 2({}^{n}C_{2}+2)={}^{n}C_{1}+{}^{n}C_{3}+2n \\ 2^{n}C_{2}+4={}^{n}C_{3}+3n \\ \Rightarrow n^{3}-9n^{2}+26n-24=0 \\ \Rightarrow n=2,3,4 \\ \Rightarrow \text{Sum of all value of}n\text{is}9 \end{array}$

text:
Let $y=y(x)$ be the solution of the differential equation $x^{4}\mathrm{d}y+\left (4x^{3}y+2\sin x\right )\mathrm{d}x=0,x>0,y\left (\frac{π}{2}\right )=0$.

Then $π^{4}y\left (\frac{π}{3}\right )$ is equal to :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 23rd January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Since $x^{4}\quad dy+4x^{3}ydx=d\left (x^{4}y\right )$, the equation is

$d\left (x^{4}y\right )=-2\sin xdx\Rightarrow x^{4}y=2\cos x+c$

At $x=\dfrac{π}{2}$, $y=0$: $0=2\cos \dfrac{π}{2}+c$, so $c=0$ and $x^{4}y=2\cos x$.

At $x=\dfrac{π}{3}$: $\dfrac{π^{4}}{81}y\left (\dfrac{π}{3}\right )=2\cos \dfrac{π}{3}=1$, so

$π^{4}\quad y\left (\dfrac{π}{3}\right )=81$

Hence, the correct option is (D).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2026 (Online) 23rd January Morning Shift

text: Let $\mathrm{A}=\{-2,-1,0,1,2,3,4\}$. Let R be a relation on A defined by $x\mathrm{R}y$ if and only if $2x+y⩽2$. Let $l$ be the number of elements in R . Let m and n be the minimum number of elements required to be added in R to make it reflexive and symmetric relations respectively. Then $l+\mathrm{m}+\mathrm{n}$ is equal to :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 23rd January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$A=\{-2,-1,0,1,2,3,4\}$ and $xRy⟺y\leq 2-2x$.

Values of $y\in A$ for each $x$: $x=-2$: $y\leq 6$, 7 values; $x=-1$: $y\leq 4$, 7 values; $x=0$: $y\leq 2$, 5 values; $x=1$: $y\leq 0$, 3 values; $x=2$: $y\leq -2$, 1 value; $x=3,4$: none. So $l=7+7+5+3+1=23$.

$(x,x)\in R⟺3x\leq 2⟺x\leq 0$, so $(1,1),(2,2),(3,3),(4,4)$ must be added: $m=4$.

For symmetry, every $(x,y)\in R$ with $2y+x>2$ needs $(y,x)$ added. These pairs are $(-2,3),(-2,4)$ from $x=-2$; $(-1,2),(-1,3),(-1,4)$ from $x=-1$; $(0,2)$ from $x=0$; none from $x=1,2$. The pairs to add are $(3,-2),(4,-2),(2,-1),(3,-1),(4,-1),(2,0)$: $n=6$.

$l+m+n=23+4+6=33$

Hence, the correct option is (C).

text: Let $f(x)=\left \{\begin{array}{ll} \frac{\mathrm{a}x^{2}+2\mathrm{a}x+3}{4x^{2}+4x-3} & ,x\neq -\frac{3}{2},\frac{1}{2} \\ \mathrm{b} & ,x=-\frac{3}{2},\frac{1}{2} \end{array} \right.$ be continuous at $x=-\frac{3}{2}$. If $f\circ f(x)=\frac{7}{5}$, then $x$ is equal to:
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 23rd January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$\begin{array}{l} \lim _{x\to \frac{-3}{2}}\dfrac{ax^{2}+2ax+3}{4x^{2}+4x-3}=b \\ ax^{2}+2ax+3=0\text{at}x=\dfrac{-3}{2} \\ \Rightarrow \dfrac{9a}{4}-3a+3=0 \\ \Rightarrow \dfrac{3a}{4}=3 \\ \Rightarrow a=4 \\ \lim _{x\to \frac{-3}{2}}\dfrac{4x^{2}+8x+3}{4x^{2}+4x-3} \end{array}$

$\begin{array}{l} =\lim _{x\to \frac{-3}{2}}\dfrac{(2x+1)(2x+3)}{(2x-1)(2x+3)} \\ =\dfrac{-2}{-4}=\dfrac{1}{2}=b \\ \therefore f(x)=\dfrac{2x+1}{2x-1} \\ f(f(x))=\dfrac{7}{5} \\ \therefore \quad \dfrac{2f(x)+1}{2f(x)-1}=\dfrac{7}{5} \\ \Rightarrow f(x)=3 \\ \dfrac{2x+1}{2x-1}=3 \\ \Rightarrow x=1 \end{array}$

text:
Let $|\mathrm{A}|=6$, where A is a $3\times 3$ matrix. If $\left |\mathrm{adj}\left (3\mathrm{adj}\left (\mathrm{A}^{2}\cdot \mathrm{adj}(2\mathrm{A})\right )\right )\right |=2^{\mathrm{m}}\cdot 3^{\mathrm{n}},\mathrm{m},\mathrm{n}\in 𝐍$, then $\mathrm{m}+\mathrm{n}$ is equal to

$____$ .
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 23rd January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Let  

$X=A^{2}\cdot \mathrm{adj}(2A)$

so the given expression is

$|\mathrm{adj}(3\mathrm{adj}(X))|.$

Since $A$ is a $3\times 3$ matrix and $|A|=6$:

Step 1: Find $|A^{2}|$
$|A^{2}|=|A|^{2}=6^{2}=36$

Step 2: Find $|\mathrm{adj}(2A)|$
First,

$|2A|=2^{3}|A|=8\cdot 6=48$

For a $3\times 3$ matrix $M$,

$|\mathrm{adj}(M)|=|M|^{3-1}=|M|^{2}$

So,

$|\mathrm{adj}(2A)|=|2A|^{2}=48^{2}$

Step 3: Find $|X|$
$|X|=|A^{2}|\cdot |\mathrm{adj}(2A)|=36\cdot 48^{2}$

Now,

$36=2^{2}\cdot 3^{2},48=2^{4}\cdot 3$

So,

$48^{2}=2^{8}\cdot 3^{2}$

Hence,

$|X|=(2^{2}\cdot 3^{2})(2^{8}\cdot 3^{2})=2^{10}\cdot 3^{4}$

Step 4: Find $|3\mathrm{adj}(X)|$
First,

$|\mathrm{adj}(X)|=|X|^{2}=(2^{10}\cdot 3^{4})^{2}=2^{20}\cdot 3^{8}$

Since $3\mathrm{adj}(X)$ is a $3\times 3$ matrix,

$|3\mathrm{adj}(X)|=3^{3}\cdot |\mathrm{adj}(X)|$

Therefore,

$|3\mathrm{adj}(X)|=27\cdot 2^{20}\cdot 3^{8}=2^{20}\cdot 3^{11}$

Step 5: Find the required determinant
Again using

$|\mathrm{adj}(M)|=|M|^{2}$

we get

$|\mathrm{adj}(3\mathrm{adj}(X))|=\left (2^{20}\cdot 3^{11}\right )^{2}=2^{40}\cdot 3^{22}$

So,

$m=40,n=22$

and

$m+n=40+22=62$

$62$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2026 (Online) 23rd January Morning Shift

text: Let the area of the region bounded by the curve $y=\max \{\sin x,\cos x\}$, lines $x=0,x=\frac{3π}{2}$, and the $x$-axis be A . Then, $\mathrm{A}+\mathrm{A}^{2}$ is equal to $____$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 23rd January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
On $\left [0,\frac{3π}{2}\right ]$, $\cos x\geq \sin x$ on $\left [0,\frac{π}{4}\right ]$ and $\left [\frac{5π}{4},\frac{3π}{2}\right ]$, and $\sin x\geq \cos x$ on $\left [\frac{π}{4},\frac{5π}{4}\right ]$. So $y=\cos x$, $\sin x$, $\cos x$ on these three intervals.

The curve is above the $x$-axis on $[0,π]$ and below it on $\left (π,\frac{3π}{2}\right )$, since $\sin x<0$ on $\left (π,\frac{5π}{4}\right ]$ and $\cos x\leq 0$ on $\left [\frac{5π}{4},\frac{3π}{2}\right ]$.

$A=\int\limits _{0}^{π/4}\cos xdx+\int\limits _{π/4}^{π}\sin xdx-\int\limits _{π}^{5π/4}\sin xdx-\int\limits _{5π/4}^{3π/2}\cos xdx$

$=\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}+\left (1+\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\right )+\left (1-\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\right )+\left (1-\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\right )=3$

$A+A^{2}=3+9=12$.

Hence, the answer is 12.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2026 (Online) 23rd January Morning Shift

text: Let $f$ be a twice differentiable non-negative function such that $(f(x))^{2}=25+\int\limits _{0}^{x}\left ((f(\mathrm{t}))^{2}+(f^{'}(\mathrm{t}))^{2}\right )\mathrm{dt}$. Then the mean of $f(\log _{\mathrm{e}}(1)),f(\log _{\mathrm{e}}(2)),\ldots ..,f(\log _{\mathrm{e}}(625))$ is equal to $____$ .
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 23rd January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Let $y=f(x)$

$y^{2}=25+\int\limits _{0}^{x}\left (f(t)^{2}+f^{'}(t)^{2}\right )dt$

Differentiating w.r.t. $x$

$\begin{array}{l} 2y\dfrac{dy}{dx}=y^{2}+\left (\dfrac{dy}{dx}\right )^{2} \\ \Rightarrow \left (\dfrac{dy}{dx}-y\right )^{2}=0\Rightarrow \dfrac{dy}{y}=dx \\ \Rightarrow \ln |y|=x+c \end{array}$

Such that

$\begin{array}{l} f(0)^{2}=25+\int\limits _{0}^{0}\left (f^{2}(t)+f^{'}(t)^{2}\right )dt \\ \Rightarrow f(0)=5 \\ \Rightarrow \ln 5=c \end{array}$

$\begin{array}{l} \Rightarrow \ln |y|=x+\ln 5 \\ \Rightarrow y=5e^{x} \\ f(\ln k)=5e^{\ln k}=5k \\ \text{Mean of}\{5,10,\ldots 625\times 5\} \\ =\dfrac{(5+10+\ldots 5\times 625)}{625}=\dfrac{5(625)(626)}{625\times 2} \\ =5\times 313 \\ =1565 \end{array}$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2026 (Online) 23rd January Morning Shift

text:
From the first 100 natural numbers, two numbers first $a$ and then $b$ are selected randomly without replacement. If the probability that $\mathrm{a}-\mathrm{b}⩾10$ is $\frac{\mathrm{m}}{\mathrm{n}},\gcd (\mathrm{m},\mathrm{n})=1$, then $\mathrm{m}+\mathrm{n}$ is equal to

$____$ .
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 23rd January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Since $a$ is selected first and then $b$, the outcomes are ordered pairs of distinct numbers: $100\times 99=9900$.

For $a-b\geq 10$, $b$ can be at most $90$. For $b=k$ with $1\leq k\leq 90$, $a$ can be $k+10,k+11,\ldots ,100$, that is $91-k$ values: $90$ values for $b=1$, $89$ for $b=2$, and so on down to $1$ value for $b=90$.

$\text{Favourable outcomes}=90+89+\cdots +1=\dfrac{90\times 91}{2}=4095$

$P=\dfrac{4095}{9900}=\dfrac{91}{220}$

Since $91=7\times 13$ and $220=2^{2}\times 5\times 11$, $\gcd (91,220)=1$, so $m=91$, $n=220$ and $m+n=311$.

Hence, the answer is 311.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2026 (Online) 23rd January Morning Shift
